clinician.final_diagnosis: ocular Toxoplasmosis involving his right eye
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 38-year-old male presented with 5-day history of decreased vision in the right eye (BCVA 18/20). Ophthalmologic examination revealed vitritis (positive atrial flashes, light vitreous turbidity) and classic fundus findings of ocular toxoplasmosis: an active yellow-white retinochoroidal lesion (1.5 disc sizes) with poorly defined borders located inferior to a pigmented old scar (2 disc sizes) in the temporal arcade. SD-OCT confirmed neuroepithelial edema with serous detachment in the active lesion and atrophy in the old lesion. Aqueous humor and serum sampling performed. After 3 days, laboratory confirmation established the diagnosis: aqueous humor PCR positive for Toxoplasma DNA, positive local antibody production (Goldmann-Witmer coefficient 12, reference 0-2), and positive serum Toxoplasma IgG (10.04 IU/mL). Infectious differential diagnoses were excluded (negative HIV, HSV, VZV, CMV, and syphilis serology).

Local intraocular antibody production demonstrated by elevated Goldmann-Witmer coefficient (12, reference range 0-2), specific for ocular toxoplasmosis

Clinical presentation consistent with ocular toxoplasmosis: unilateral decreased vision with vitritis and active retinochoroidal lesion adjacent to old scar (headlight in fog appearance)
SD-OCT findings of neuroepithelial edema and serous detachment in active lesion supporting inflammatory activity
Exclusion of other infectious etiologies (HIV, Herpes simplex, Varicella zoster, CMV, and syphilis)
